source: LQ-20261107-2148 (Home v010 APPROVED 2026-11-11; HOME-BACKEND-SPEC-20261111 section LQ-2148). Read by scripts/lib/lane_health.py; an unreadable file falls back to the module DEFAULTS and the snapshot names the gap.

notes.late_grace_minutes: spec test: a slot done 20 min late with a 10-min grace is late 1. Lateness is started_at - slot; the slot is matched on the dispatch (requested_at).
notes.stale_after_slots: output signal older than the lane's 3rd-newest expected slot (about 2.5x cadence, the spec's freshness-contract multiple), counted on the lane's own market-day/active-day slots so a weekend is not stale.
notes.business_critical_value_classes: LQ-2967 (REVIEW-2963 D2): the Schedulers WARN counts only LATE/STALE/FAILING lanes whose lane_registry value_class is in this list. Empty meant every lane counted, so on the live registry the tile read WARN permanently (33 lanes LATE/STALE/FAILING on 2026-11-13, most a late start under host load). 'Business Critical' is the registry's top tier (66 lanes). 'Operationally Important' (192 lanes, 18 off schedule that day) is left out on purpose: a lane in it that must page is promoted to Business Critical in lane_registry.json, not listed here. Gap: Home-card owner lanes stop-health-check (Technical Debt), market-quotes-extended (UNCLASSIFIED), vix-index-quotes-schwab (no class) and deploy-detect (Nice to Have) are outside the tier, so their staleness does not turn Schedulers WARN; reclassifying them is a registry decision. Only the WARN is narrowed; unknown_states still count every lane.
notes.unknown_states: NOT_MEASURED (cron/systemd: no per-run ledger, spec A4) keeps the rollup UNKNOWN rather than OK until those lanes move to n8n. Unknown never reads as OK.
notes.stale_after_minutes: the snapshot is stale for a reader after 30 min (3 missed 10-minute slots)
